papers.title: How Can Rhetoric Reward-Hack AI Reviewers? Dissecting Rhetorical Sensitivity in AI-Based Peer Review

summary.tldr: Researchers created a controlled dataset of 4,200 rewritten ICLR manuscripts to demonstrate how content-preserving rhetorical changes systematically reward-hack AI reviewers' scoring behaviors across various evaluation conditions.
key_points: Evaluated 4,200 full-paper variants from 120 anonymized ICLR 2026 submissions across six rhetorical dimensions using two LLM rewriters and five LLM reviewers.
Evidence framing and novelty stance produced the largest positive-negative contrasts in overall assessment scores, followed by scope framing as a weaker second tier.
Score shifts depended heavily on original ratings: lower scores tended to rise, higher scores fell, and directional impacts were most distinct in middle score ranges.
Strict review protocols reduced mean overall assessment by 1.36 points without consistently altering rhetorical sensitivity, while recursive or reviewer-guided rewriting showed diminishing returns.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that LLM peer reviewers are susceptible to rhetorical reward-hacking highlights the need for evaluation systems that remain robust against stylistic manipulation of scientific papers.

papers.title: Full-bandwidth transformer

summary.tldr: The full-bandwidth transformer introduces latent feedback by fusing the previous top-layer hidden state with the next token embedding via a gated linear unit, bypassing the narrow single-token vertical bottleneck in standard autoregressive decoding.
key_points: Fuses top-layer hidden states with sampled token embeddings using a gated linear unit to allow non-verbalized computation to re-enter the transformer stack.
Preserves the standard transformer architecture, KV cache structure, and language-modeling training objective.
Uses a scheduled multi-pass training objective late in pretraining with a small fraction of deeper feedback passes to enable parallel teacher forcing and ensure stability.
Evaluated on 1B-parameter models trained on up to 400B tokens, matching or approaching standard transformers trained on 1.5x more tokens with negligible per-token overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves pretraining efficiency, downstream task performance, and produces shorter reasoning traces without requiring architecture changes, custom KV caches, or significant decoding latency.

papers.title: AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning

summary.tldr: The Agentic Video Auto-Encoder (AVA-Encoder) introduces an agent-native framework that converts videos into structured knowledge graphs and back, optimizing representations via textual gradients.
key_points: Transforms raw video into a knowledge graph (KG) containing structured text hierarchy/state nodes and a linked asset layer of images, audio, and video via typed edges.
Uses a textual-gradient optimization framework driven by video reconstruction differences for outer-loop policy pseudo-training and test-time inner-loop KG refinement.
Outperforms the strongest external baseline by 20.7 percentage points in reconstruction tasks.
Reaches superior performance over human-tuned policies in a policy-only setting while using 74.3% fewer system-prompt tokens.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a structured, agent-interpretable video format that enables creative AI agents to better reason about, query, and edit cinematic-grade video content.

papers.title: OmniScientist: An Omni-Modal Omni-Discipline AI Scientist

summary.tldr: OmniScientist is an end-to-end AI scientist framework that conducts multidisciplinary research directly from raw, omni-modal evidence across an entire autonomous pipeline.
key_points: Architecture features a perception layer and three autonomous agents (ideation, experiment, writeup) operating within a deterministic pipeline with code-based idea, rigour, and claim checks.
Evaluated on 36 real-data cases covering 5 discipline families, using diverse modalities including images, signals, audio, video, 3D structures, trajectories, tables, formulae, and graphs.
Achieved a 100% completion rate from raw data to compiled manuscript across all 36 test cases, with a mean paper score of 6.3 using the reference reasoning backbone.
Outperformed a blind scalar-only variant in 85% of paired comparisons, demonstrating improvements across all 7 evaluation dimensions through direct modal perception.
summary.why_it_matters: Direct multimodal perception across the full research lifecycle prevents the information loss of precomputed text or scalar summaries, enabling accurate AI-driven scientific discovery from raw experimental data.

papers.title: SKILLER: Language-Level Reinforcement Learning for Reusable Skill Extraction in Small Language Models

summary.tldr: SKILLER is a natural-language-driven reinforcement learning framework that uses a strong model as actor-critic to automatically generate reusable, executor-specific skills for small language models.
key_points: Treats the small-model agent system as the environment while propagating all reinforcement learning signals entirely via natural language.
Uses a strong model to act as both actor and critic during the language-level reinforcement learning process.
Evaluated using Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.5-4B across five benchmarks, yielding absolute gains of 4.3 to 20.4 percentage points on the 9B model and 1.8 to 13.3 points on the 4B model.
Matches the performance of strong closed-source models on single-skill tasks in SkillsBench.
summary.why_it_matters: It drastically reduces deployment costs by enabling open-source small language models running on consumer GPUs to match closed-source model performance via automatically generated skill constraints.

papers.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning

summary.tldr: Perturbed Parameter Policy Optimization (3PO) enables parameter-space exploration in LLM reinforcement learning by sampling diverse policy weights from a posterior to improve reasoning and code generation performance over GRPO.
key_points: Introduces 3PO, a family of methods that samples parameter-space policies from a posterior to complement traditional action-space token temperature scaling.
Uses varied parameter sampling strategies and rollout grouping techniques to optimize reward estimation without adding significant FLOP overhead.
Evaluated on OLMo-3-1025-7B and Qwen2.5-Math-7B models across mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks.
Reduces the occurrence of zero-advantage groups and malformed or incorrect rollouts during training compared to standard GRPO and action-space baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: Parameter-space exploration prevents training stalls and divergence in LLM reinforcement learning by generating structurally diverse rollouts that action-space temperature scaling cannot achieve.

papers.title: Context-Matched Distillation: Teacher Causality for Autoregressive Video Distillation

summary.tldr: Context-Matched Distillation (CMD) aligns video distillation by using a causal teacher that evaluates targets without future frame or control access, ensuring teacher supervision matches the student's autoregressive information set.
key_points: Identifies a mis-alignment in conventional video distribution matching distillation (DMD), where bidirectional teachers supervise causal few-step students using future frames and controls.
Initializes the student from the same causal teacher model to maintain temporal consistency across training, distillation, and inference.
Introduces Prefix Scoring to evaluate generated targets against their realized student-generated prefix via prefix caching.
Applies Prefix Corruption to perturb unreliable early-stage prefixes while maintaining target-context alignment.
Supports frame-wise, chunk-wise, long video, and camera-conditioned autoregressive generation.
summary.why_it_matters: CMD enables low-latency, few-step autoregressive video generation that achieves state-of-the-art performance and higher fidelity to real-time, time-varying user controls.

papers.title: LycheeMemory V2: Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents via Semantic Segment-Level Consolidation

summary.tldr: LycheeMemory V2 replaces turn-level LLM memory consolidation with semantic segment-level consolidation, batching exchanges to drastically reduce token costs while preserving detailed temporal and event evidence.
key_points: Batches interaction history into semantic segments rather than invoking LLM consolidation after every turn.
Uses semantic boundary detection instead of fixed-window batching to maintain coherent event-level context.
Encodes finalized segments into context-independent typed memory records using lightweight structured indexes for query retrieval.
Achieves SOTA performance with GPT-4.1-Mini, scoring 89.22% on LoCoMo and 92.20% on LongMemEval-S.
Reduces construction tokens compared to A-Mem by 86.0% on LoCoMo and 75.9% on LongMemEval-S without raising query-time token costs.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that optimizing memory consolidation granularity significantly lowers LLM agent operating costs without compromising retrieval accuracy or adding query overhead.

papers.title: Hybrid-Policy Self-Editing for Composable Unstructured Knowledge Editing

summary.tldr: HPSE introduces a self-distillation framework that uses hybrid rollouts to edit unstructured knowledge in LLMs, improving multi-hop reasoning and atomic fact extraction.
key_points: Identifies composability failure in unstructured knowledge editing (UKE), where models recall edited passages but fail at multi-hop reasoning or answering atomic questions.
Formulates knowledge editing as proactive self-distillation from a privileged in-context state of the target LLM without requiring external supervision.
Combines off-policy steps to insert missing facts where model coverage fails with on-policy generation elsewhere to form a hybrid rollout strategy.
Demonstrates plug-and-play performance gains across four LLM backbones and two knowledge editors.
summary.why_it_matters: HPSE enables updated LLMs to perform multi-hop reasoning over new unstructured text updates without full retraining or supervised target datasets.

papers.title: Thought-Level Beam Search for Reasoning

summary.tldr: Gambit is a thought-level beam search algorithm that dynamically concentrates inference compute onto promising reasoning trajectories via a lightweight hidden-state scorer while maintaining high hardware utilization.
key_points: Addresses test-time reasoning as a constrained compute allocation problem over partial trajectories, bypassing memory bottlenecks of parallel sampling and hardware starvation of subtractive pruning.
Periodically prunes unpromising trajectories and immediately branches from high-quality reasoning prefixes using a lightweight hidden-state probe.
Outperforms pruning baselines under identical hardware constraints, adding up to +6.7% absolute accuracy on HMMT-24 and +3.3% on AIME-25.
Delivers over 2x higher throughput on trace completion and reduces total token consumption by up to 68.5% compared to standard parallel sampling.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves reasoning model performance and throughput under fixed hardware budgets while drastically reducing token consumption.

papers.title: ReRound: Reconstructive Rounding to Resolve Midpoint Ambiguity in Calibration-Free LLM Quantization

summary.tldr: ReRound introduces a calibration-free quantization method that uses a conditional diffusion model to guide round-to-nearest decisions for weight values near interval midpoints.
key_points: Trains a conditional diffusion model to generate continuous weight reconstructions that act as guidance signals for ambiguous rounding decisions near quantization midpoints.
Uses a tolerance metric to apply diffusion-guided rounding within a midpoint tolerance region while using standard round-to-nearest (RTN) for weights near quantization boundaries.
Selects the optimal tolerance parameter by picking the candidate de-quantized weight matrix whose leading singular values most closely match the full-precision weights.
Outperforms standard RTN and calibration-free methods for 3-bit and 4-bit weight quantization, especially on smaller LLMs, without adding inference runtime overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves low-bit weight quantization accuracy for small LLMs entirely offline without requiring calibration data or adding inference runtime latency.

papers.title: Are You Sure You're Sure? On the Impact of Instruction Tuning on Confidence and Lexical Diversity

summary.tldr: Instruction tuning consistently alters model verbalized confidence and decreases cross-rationale diversity without improving predictive accuracy or likelihood-based calibration.
key_points: Evaluation across three matched base and instruction-tuned model pairs shows that instruction tuning shifts answer confidence despite producing limited changes in predictive accuracy.
Instruction tuning reduces likelihood-based calibration in question-answering benchmarks.
Cross-rationale diversity consistently decreases post-tuning, while surface-level lexical diversity exhibits variable changes across different models and benchmarks.
Observed differences in confidence and rationale diversity persist even after controlling for answer selection and rationale length.
summary.why_it_matters: Instruction tuning can induce verbalized overconfidence and reduce rationale variety without delivering corresponding gains in underlying model accuracy or calibration.

papers.title: From Atomic Evidence to Logical Composition: Structured Compositional Reasoning over Compound Answer Options

summary.tldr: A new framework decomposes compound answer options into atomic judgments, scoring contrastive hypotheses and using an operator-constrained integer linear program to compose predictions without directly exposing compound options to LLMs.
key_points: Addresses LLM failure on compound options using AND, OR, and NEITHER/NOR operators even when individual atomic judgments are correct.
Decomposes compound options into atomic components, evaluates them via contrastive hypotheses, and uses an operator-constrained integer linear program (ILP) for calibrated score composition.
Introduces LOGICAL-SATA, a reading-comprehension benchmark derived from SATA-Bench, alongside evaluations on LOGICAL-COMMONSENSEQA.
Improves Macro-F1 from 48.3 to 77.0 on human-validated LOGICAL-COMMONSENSEQA and from 47.0 to 75.6 on LOGICAL-SATA, achieving the largest performance gains on NEITHER/NOR operators.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLMs to reliably solve complex logical multiple-choice questions by replacing direct end-to-end guessing with explicit atomic scoring and structured optimization.

papers.title: Specification-first convergence with an AI coding agent: a case study of dismantling a core architectural invariant across 189 files in a 717k-line codebase with no test oracle and no human code review

summary.tldr: An AI agent successfully completed a large-scale architectural refactoring across 189 files in a 717k-line codebase using a specification-first protocol with zero human code review or pre-existing test oracle.
key_points: The refactoring dismantled a core lifetime UI invariant in a 717,725-line, 3,648-file TypeScript application, spanning 288 files modified, 34,770 insertions, and 16,422 deletions.

The protocol utilized formal agent-written specifications, 14 refinement audit cycles against source code, atomic implementation, a compile/test loop, and 17 verification cycles auditing code against the frozen specification.
Across 31 total audit passes, the agent corrected 201 defects prior to human execution, converging when two consecutive verification passes returned zero findings.
The entire process took three days and USD 2,430 in API costs, resulting in zero observed bugs across subsequent usage sessions.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that AI coding agents can safely execute massive, cross-cutting architectural changes without human code review by using rigorous, multi-pass specification audits as a replacement for conventional test oracles.

papers.title: Ready Cohorts: Bounding GPU Opportunity and Avoiding Host Round Trips in LLM-Agent Control

summary.tldr: A study formalizes ready-cohort boundaries for LLM-agent GPU control, demonstrating that exact packing captures 43% of offline opportunity and keeping binary route decisions on-device yields up to 2.39x speedups without host round trips.
key_points: Formalizes the ready-cohort boundary using fixed-partition share (F), exact offline share (P*), local upper bound (U), and online achieved share (A).

Evaluation on an 851-session trace at 100k active sessions and a 50 ms launch deadline yields F=30.19%, P*=43.00%, and U=45.85%, where exact packing recovers 81.83% of the opportunity lost to fixed windows.
Retaining a GPU-computed 4-byte binary route decision on-device rather than returning it to the host produces speedup ratios from 1.19x to 2.39x across 36 GPU configurations.

All 14,557,440 tested batched invocations across admissible mechanisms perfectly matched a host oracle, whereas fixed nested device graphs without host decision removal were slower in all 60 tested configurations.
summary.why_it_matters: Establishing GPU-resident control paths and deadline-feasible cohort packing allows LLM-agent services to drastically reduce host-device communication overhead and offload control execution efficiently.

papers.title: Beyond Final Scores: A Systematic Evaluation of Agents for Long-Horizon AI Research and Development

summary.tldr: A new evaluation framework assesses seven frontier models across 36 long-horizon tasks, analyzing within-run process behavior and experience reuse rather than relying solely on final task scores.
key_points: Evaluates seven frontier models across 36 long-horizon AI research and development tasks.
Introduces a evaluation framework using rule-based metrics to analyze Solution Framing, Execution, and Feedback Control.
Assesses experience reuse within and across tasks using controlled comparisons, revealing that experience can either aid or mislead subsequent decisions.
Finds that agents behave as engineering optimizers rather than autonomous researchers, excelling at adapting established techniques while rarely producing genuine methodological novelty.
Identifies distinct process bottlenecks and harness design choices as major factors driving performance variability across runs.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating intermediate agent behaviors and experience management reveals hidden failure modes, guiding better model training, inference strategies, and harness design for long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: Training AI Scientists to Replicate Research

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced Replica, a task space for paper replication using an auto-generated rubric-based judge, and post-trained Faraday, a 27B-parameter AI scientist agent that out-performs Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5.
key_points: Replica provides a scalable task space for paper replication using a low-noise, rubric-based judge that aligns with human evaluations.
Faraday is a 27B-parameter post-trained agent that utilizes coding agents as tools to perform replication tasks.
Faraday outperforms Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 on held-out replication benchmarks while adopting a scientifically-principled approach.
summary.why_it_matters: Automating paper replication with reliable reward signals enables AI agents to conduct long-horizon scientific research without complex external harnesses.

papers.title: CROP: Task Relevance via Counterfactuals for Selective On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Counterfactual Relevance for On-Policy Distillation (CROP) filters token-level supervision in on-policy distillation by measuring a prompt's counterfactual sensitivity margin calibrated against meaning-preserving paraphrases.
key_points: CROP constructs validated original-paraphrase-counterfactual prompt triplets while keeping student rollouts fixed to evaluate token-level task relevance.
Supervision value is computed as a response position's sensitivity to task-relevant counterfactual changes, calibrated by its sensitivity to paraphrased rewrites.
Component analysis validates that both counterfactual sensitivity and paraphrase calibration contribute to selective supervision performance over random or lowest-relevance baselines.
CROP achieves performance improvements of 1.92 and 2.96 points over the strongest non-CROP selective baseline across two teacher-student setups.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes task relevance as an effective, model-internal criterion for allocating token-level supervision in selective on-policy language model distillation.

papers.title: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation (LOPD) makes a self-teacher's privileged context learnable end-to-end via continuous latent tokens composed from retrieved experiences, replacing hand-crafted privileged artifacts.
key_points: LOPD retrieves relevant past experiences and converts them into continuous latent tokens to condition a self-teacher.
The student model generates trajectories from task history and receives dense, token-level supervision from the teacher at every visited prefix.
Introduces a privileged-margin objective to regulate and stabilize the learning of the latent contextual tokens.
Outperforms RLVR, traditional OPSD, SDPO, and Skill-SD on agentic tool use and code generation benchmarks.
Achieves higher learning efficiency than GRPO and Skill-SD while requiring under 30% of their rollout budget.
summary.why_it_matters: LOPD reduces reliance on human-designed feedback structures, enabling self-evolving AI agents to continuously improve performance and sample efficiency through autonomous, end-to-end experience learning.

papers.title: I-SDPO: Instance-Level Adaptive Self-Distillation Policy Optimization

summary.tldr: I-SDPO dynamically routes training objectives by using privileged self-distillation for all-incorrect rollout groups and standard GRPO for any-success groups, eliminating optimization bias as policy capability improves.
key_points: Addresses GRPO's failure mode where uninformative all-incorrect rollout groups lack relative reward signals.
Applies instance-level routing across a rollout group to restrict privileged self-distillation strictly to zero-success instances.
Provides a local theoretical analysis showing that non-vanishing biased distillation weights create an optimization bias floor.
Automatically decreases the expected distillation rate as success probability grows without requiring a manual schedule.
Increases average mean@16 accuracy on SciKnowEval from 56.67% (GRPO) to 70.31%, with a peak domain gain of 18.24 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves reinforcement learning from AI feedback by providing dense supervision on hard instances while avoiding performance ceilings caused by persistent teacher bias.

papers.title: QuoteBench: How Matched Scores Can Hide Command-Path Failures

summary.tldr: QuoteBench shows that matched LLM coding agent execution scores obscure severe transport-level parsing failures, which models must actively compensate for via boundary adaptation.
key_points: Evaluates 56 one-shot tasks across 14 incident-derived families using exact final-state validation to isolate command-generation errors from execution transport parsing failures.
Passing raw model outputs through an added unescaped transport parser degrades task success rates by 55.4 to 73.2 percentage points across eight configurations.
Disclosing the execution boundary to the model recovers 30.4 to 60.7 percentage points for six configurations, while failing to help two others.
GPT-5.6-sol exhibits a net matched gap of only -3.6 points, hiding -64.3 points of parser damage and +60.7 points of prompt-driven model compensation.
Execution path details reorder model benchmark rankings, introducing one unambiguous reversal among 26 comparable model pairs.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluations must explicitly report generation contracts and transport execution paths, as raw execution scores fail to reflect intrinsic model capabilities.

papers.title: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically Controlled Knowledge Exposure

summary.tldr: Researchers created LITTLECURRICULUM, an 88B-token elementary-level corpus, and LITTLELEARNER, a 5B-parameter model trained from scratch on it, establishing a pedagogically restricted sandbox for studying LLM knowledge acquisition.
key_points: LITTLECURRICULUM is a 88-billion-token pretraining corpus strictly limited to U.S. elementary material (Grade 5 and below).
LITTLELEARNER is a 5-billion-parameter LLM pretrained from scratch on LITTLECURRICULUM to establish clear knowledge and capability boundaries.
Initial experiments on post-training and in-context learning demonstrated improved utilization of existing model knowledge without elevating out-of-scope capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: The model and corpus provide a controlled environment to study how LLMs acquire and represent knowledge without the interference of uncharacterized web-scale training data.

papers.title: Vero: Can AI Agents Build Formally Verified Software Repositories?

summary.tldr: Vero is the first benchmark for evaluating joint implementation and formal proof synthesis at the repository level, containing 43 multi-module Lean 4 instances sourced from real-world software across four programming languages.
key_points: Vero spans domains like cryptography and distributed systems, using multi-module Lean 4 repositories with preset API interfaces, formal specifications, and reference implementations.
Supports both proof-only and joint code-and-proof evaluation modes, alongside an audit mechanism to detect specification or reference code errors.
Evaluated frontier coding agents with Lean toolchain access solved at most 27 of 43 instances, failing completely on the hardest repositories.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a benchmark proving that state-of-the-art AI agents currently struggle to generate formally verified, correct code across complex, multi-module repositories.

papers.title: The data geometry of masking diffusion: Certified-optimal schedules via unmasking growth complexity

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced Unmasking Growth Complexity (UGC), a data geometry measure that bounds discrete masking diffusion KL error to enable certified-optimal unmasking schedules.
key_points: Unmasking Growth Complexity (UGC) local increments directly control KL discretization error across Bernoulli-subset and fixed-cardinality schemes.
UGC increments can be estimated directly from data samples via KL increments along coupled reveal trajectories.
The framework provides certified-optimal samplers that achieve target KL errors with high probability and iteration complexity within a constant factor of oracle procedures.
In the fine-partition limit, the squared integral of the square-root UGC density sets the leading-order optimal Euler discretization error.
Adaptive multi-block schedules utilizing UGC achieve up to \tilde{\Omega}(\sqrt{d}) dimension-dependent efficiency gains over non-adaptive schedules using a constant number of blocks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables sample-based optimization of discrete diffusion sampling schedules, achieving guaranteed accuracy bounds while reducing required computational steps by up to a factor of \tilde{\Omega}(\sqrt{d}).

papers.title: DFM Mimir v1: An Open HRM Delivering Frontier Performance at 1B Parameters Using Only Permissible Post-Training Data

summary.tldr: DFM Mimir v1 is an open 1-billion-parameter Hierarchical Reasoning Model trained from scratch using exclusively permissible post-training data, achieving state-of-the-art results for Danish and competitive performance in English, Math, and Code.
key_points: Built on the 1B-parameter Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM) architecture and trained from scratch.
Post-training relies strictly on a permissible mixture of 161 datasets.
Outperforms the original HRM-Text 1B and rivals larger models including Qwen 3.5 4B and Gemma 4 E2B across 20 benchmarks.
Sets a new state of the art for Danish language performance while maintaining strong performance in English, Math, and Code.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that a 1B-parameter model trained entirely on ethically sourced, permissible data can match or exceed the performance of much larger frontier models.

security.title: Understanding Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Vertical Federated Learning: The Gap Between Research and Practice

summary.tldr: A new paper identifies unrealistic assumptions in current Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) backdoor attack and defense research and introduces BVBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate vulnerabilities under practical constraints.
key_points: Identifies a gap between VFL research and real-world practice caused by attacks relying on unrealistic prior knowledge and flawed evaluation methods.
Redefines VFL threat models to account for practical operational constraints and asymmetric information structures where the initiator withholds task details.
Proposes realistic backdoor workflows for training-time poisoning and inference-time activation by malicious contributors.
Introduces BVBench, a comprehensive backdoor-centric benchmark preloaded with state-of-the-art baselines for realistic VFL security evaluation.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that existing VFL backdoor defenses and attack models are fragile under realistic conditions, requiring a shift toward practical vulnerability assessments.

security.title: Beyond Visual Evidence: Revealing and Mitigating Relational Privacy Leakage in Document MLLMs

summary.tldr: Researchers identified relational privacy leakage in document MLLMs when visual evidence is scarce and introduced the Dynamic Relational Unlearning Framework (DRUF) alongside the DocPrivacyBench benchmark to mitigate it.
key_points: Document MLLMs performing Key Information Extraction (KIE) infer missing sensitive fields using memorized field relations when visual evidence is absent or minimal.
The Dynamic Relational Unlearning Framework (DRUF) combines a Relational Decoupling Unlearning (RDU) module with a dynamic set update mechanism to suppress high-risk field pair leakage.
DocPrivacyBench was created to evaluate privacy leakage susceptibility and utility preservation across three MLLMs and six unlearning baselines.
DRUF improved privacy leakage suppression by 4.8 percentage points over the strongest baseline while preserving document extraction utility.
summary.why_it_matters: This work enables identity document processing MLLMs to reduce sensitive personal data exposure caused by training data memorization without degrading key extraction accuracy.

security.title: Adversarial Robustness in Smishing Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Adversarial Fragility in Classical vs. Transformer-Based Detection Systems

summary.tldr: A comparative study shows transformer-based smishing detectors resist adversarial attacks far better than classical models, though high clean-text accuracy does not guarantee adversarial robustness.
key_points: Evaluated 27,037 messages across classical models (Random Forest, XGBoost, CNN+BiLSTM) and multilingual transformers (mBERT, XLM-RoBERTa) using three attack types and intensity levels.
Classical models faced near-catastrophic failure under character obfuscation and structural perturbation with a Robustness Degradation Ratio (RDR) up to 0.988.
Multilingual transformers exhibited higher resilience with RDR capped at 0.351, identifying structural perturbation as their primary vulnerability.
XLM-RoBERTa achieved higher clean-text baseline accuracy than mBERT but suffered greater overall performance degradation under adversarial testing.
Statistical significance of architectural impacts was validated using Mann-Whitney U, Friedman tests, and Cliff's d effect-size analysis.
summary.why_it_matters: Security teams cannot rely on clean-text evaluation metrics alone, requiring architecture-specific adversarial defenses for real-world smishing detection.

security.title: The energetic cost of mitigating AI attacks in cellular networks

summary.tldr: This paper characterizes the overlooked computational and energetic costs of deploying defense mechanisms against Machine Learning attacks in cellular networks like O-RAN.
key_points: Machine learning algorithms in cellular networks, such as the O-RAN Radio Intelligence Controller (RIC), are vulnerable to data manipulation attacks that degrade network performance.
Mitigation strategies successfully defend ML models but introduce additional computational overhead and energy consumption.
The study outlines trade-offs across the triad of ML accuracy, robustness, and energy efficiency.
summary.why_it_matters: Implementing AI security defenses in cellular networks can significantly increase energy consumption, forcing operators to balance model robustness against sustainability goals.

security.title: How China-Origin Vision-Language Models Move from Refusal to Reframing in State Alignment

summary.tldr: A 21,708-trial audit of nine vision-language models reveals that censorship in China-origin VLMs is migrating from explicit refusals to state-aligned reframing, driven by subject recognition rather than visual pixel detail.
key_points: Evaluated nine VLMs (seven China-origin, two non-China) across 200 core entries spanning ten sensitive topics and a seven-variant visual-abstraction probe across two prompt languages.
Across four generations of Qwen models, explicit refusal rates decreased while state-aligned framing increased, shifting state-aligned distortion into fluent reframing.
Chinese-language prompting roughly tripled the odds of state-aligned framing within every model tested, with China-origin models reframing 1.6x to 3.2x more than non-China models.
State-aligned framing peaked in text-only political commentary (36.5%) and was gated by high-level recognition of the depicted subject, persisting even when images were reduced to silhouettes.

Audit dimensions included explicit refusal, information integrity, visual grounding, state-aligned framing, language consistency, and response length, scored independently by two LLM judges and validated by human experts.
summary.why_it_matters: The transition from explicit refusals to implicit reframing removes the primary signal users rely on to detect that AI-generated information has been intentionally altered or withheld.

security.title: Operationalizing Cyber Threat Intelligence with GraphRAG

summary.tldr: Replacing naive vector retrieval with Microsoft GraphRAG enables automated cyber threat intelligence systems to generate durable detection plans focused on resilient behaviors rather than volatile indicators.
key_points: Evaluates Microsoft GraphRAG against Naive RAG using identical language models and generation prompts across nine CTI reports from four vendors.
In an APT28 case study, the GraphRAG-generated plan maintained 100% detection effectiveness after IP, domain, and hash rotation, whereas the Naive RAG plan dropped to 29% effectiveness.
GraphRAG consistently extracts higher-level, harder-to-evade behaviors from the Pyramid of Pain compared to vector-similarity retrieval.
Prompt wording during the generation stage was identified as nearly equal in importance to the choice of retrieval backend.
summary.why_it_matters: Using knowledge-graph retrieval allows security operations centers to automatically create threat hunting plans that remain effective even after attackers change basic infrastructure and file hashes.

security.title: A Comparison of Malware Image Transformations Using Grad-CAM and Hybrid Learning Models

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated Grad-CAM and HiResCAM on eight binary-to-image malware transformations, discovering that model accuracy and XAI explanation faithfulness do not align.
key_points: Evaluated eight distinct binary-to-image transformation methods using quantitative faithfulness and stability metrics for Grad-CAM and HiResCAM heatmaps.
Extracted features from Grad-CAM heatmaps using a MobileNetV2 CNN and trained a Random Forest model, achieving 0.777 test accuracy across 17 malware families (outperforming the 0.750 benchmark).
Demonstrated an inverse trade-off where image transformation techniques yielding the highest explanation faithfulness provided only mid-tier classification accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: High-performing image-based malware classifiers may rely on unfaithful visual features, requiring security analysts to carefully weigh classification accuracy against explanation reliability.

security.title: Instruction Alignment for Binary Code Representation Learning

summary.tldr: A new training approach incorporates fine-grained, debug-info-derived instruction alignment as an auxiliary objective to improve function-level binary code representation learning and retrieval accuracy.
key_points: Existing binary code representation methods focus on coarse function-level embeddings while neglecting fine-grained instruction-level correspondences.
Preliminary findings show that models finetuned for function-level similarity naturally improve instruction alignment over base pre-trained models.
The proposed method explicitly leverages compiler debug information to introduce instruction alignment as an auxiliary training objective.
Experimental results demonstrate improved retrieval accuracy and enhanced discriminative capability in similarity judgments.
summary.why_it_matters: Integrating instruction-level alignment into binary representation models yields more accurate and interpretable code embeddings for reverse engineering and security analysis tasks.

infra.title: Adaptive Verification in vLLM: DSpark confidence-scheduled verification

summary.tldr: vLLM introduced DSpark adaptive verification, which dynamically allocates draft token verification budgets per step using per-request confidence scores to maintain speculative decoding throughput gains up to batch size 256.
key_points: Uses a learned DSpark confidence head to estimate position-wise survival probabilities across drafted tokens, selecting a global top-B contiguous prefix across requests.
Calculates the optimal draft token budget (B) by maximizing expected tokens per unit step time using profiled cost tables evaluated via an np.argmax operation on the CPU.

Addresses severe acceptance decay (e.g., DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 acceptance dropping from >70% for token 1 to <10% for token 7) to prevent rejected draft tokens from consuming compute at high concurrencies.
Implemented in vLLM PR #47808 under the parameter enable_adaptive_verification.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the need to manually tune num_speculative_tokens per workload while preventing speculative decoding throughput degradation at high batch sizes.

infra.title: Serve Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, a 2.4T-Parameter Model, with Configurable Reasoning on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72

summary.tldr: Alibaba has released open weights for Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B (Qwen3.8-Max), a 2.4-trillion-parameter model optimized for deployment on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems with configurable reasoning.
key_points: Features 2.4 trillion total parameters with 95 billion activated parameters per token.
Utilizes a fine-grained mixture of experts (MoE) architecture.
Combines a hybrid of full and linear attention mechanisms.
Supports a context window of up to one million tokens.
summary.why_it_matters: It delivers near-frontier MoE model capabilities and million-token context processing to the open-weight AI ecosystem.

infra.title: Custom reward functions for multi-turn reinforcement learning with Amazon Nova Forge

summary.tldr: Amazon Nova Forge provides a Bring Your Own Orchestration (BYOO) environment using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to train LLM agents via composite, multi-turn custom reward functions.
key_points: Nova Forge supports multi-turn Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) using GRPO with either rule-based verifiable rewards or LLM-as-a-Judge grading.
BYOO allows custom reward logic to run in user-managed environments on Amazon ECS alongside serverless multi-turn RL options.
Custom reward functions optimize cumulative reward trajectories over multiple agent steps, including tool calling, code execution, and error recovery.
The customer-managed environment requires setting specific CDK configuration options (`use_custom_env` and `custom_env_id`) on SageMaker HyperPod and Amazon ECS.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables developers to optimize complex multi-turn agent behaviors and out-of-distribution generalization without relying solely on supervised fine-tuning data.

infra.title: Building agentic workflows with SageMaker AI and Bedrock AgentCore

summary.tldr: AWS details an architecture combining SageMaker AI endpoints running Qwen 3.5 9B with Bedrock AgentCore runtime and Strands Agents to build multi-agent workflows across custom and managed models.
key_points: Deploys Qwen 3.5 9B on SageMaker AI using an ml.g6e.2xlarge instance with the vLLM 0.22.1 Deep Learning Container.
Uses an Orchestrator agent powered by Claude Haiku 4.5 on Bedrock to route requests to specialized agents via the agents-as-tools pattern.
Integrates a Budget agent using Claude Sonnet 4.6 on Bedrock alongside a Financial Analysis agent using Qwen 3.5 9B over SageMaker's OpenAI-compatible API.
Deploys the complete multi-agent system into the managed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime environment.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows developers to mix managed foundation models with self-hosted, domain-specific models inside a single production agent framework without rewriting agent orchestration logic.

infra.title: Monitor on-premises and multi-cloud AI agents with AgentCore Observability

summary.tldr: AWS details a method to monitor AI agents hosted on-premises or on third-party clouds using AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) routed to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Observability.
key_points: Supports agents built with frameworks like Strands Agents, LangGraph, and CrewAI running on non-AWS environments, GCP, Azure, Amazon EKS, Amazon ECS, or Lambda.
Uses AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) auto-instrumentation running in-process to capture generative AI semantic convention spans.
Exports traces, metrics, and logs directly to the Amazon CloudWatch OTLP endpoint using IAM SigV4 authentication via access keys.
Provides centralized visibility into agent reasoning chains, tool invocations, model outputs, token usage, and hallucination monitoring across hybrid environments.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables centralized, specialized generative AI telemetry and cost governance for agents deployed outside the native Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime.

infra.title: Part 2: Amazon Bedrock cost attribution with Amazon Athena and CUDOS

summary.tldr: AWS details how to analyze Amazon Bedrock granular cost attribution by connecting CUR 2.0 IAM principal data to Amazon Athena and CUDOS dashboards.
key_points: Requires enabling 'caller identity (IAM principal) allocation data' in CUR 2.0 to populate the line_item_iam_principal column and iamPrincipal/ tags.
Enabling IAM principal data expands single CUR rows into multiple rows per principal, increasing S3 storage requirements for high-volume workloads.
CUR 2.0 exports should be configured with hourly time granularity and overwrite delivery options to maintain maximum detail without duplicating files.
An open-source repo (sample-cur-iam-principal-bedrock-tracking) provides an agent.md workflow to automate Athena setup using tools like Claude Code or Kiro-CLI.
summary.why_it_matters: Organizations can now perform SQL queries and view pre-built dashboards to attribute Amazon Bedrock usage and costs directly to specific IAM principals, applications, or teams.

summary.tldr: Anthropic is adopting Google DeepMind's SynthID-Text watermarking technique for future Claude models to comply with the EU AI Act.
key_points: The watermarking method uses a secret key combined with preceding text to deterministically drive the randomness used when selecting candidate tokens.
Statistical detection works by analyzing whether a generated word sequence matches the selection patterns produced by the specific key.
The approach restricts selection to valid token candidates, avoiding low-probability or obscure vocabulary choices to maintain output fidelity.
Internal testing and side-by-side human evaluation showed no impact on content quality, creativity, readability, or user ratings.
summary.why_it_matters: Text watermarking allows accurate detection of Claude-generated content without degrading the quality, readability, or creativity of the model's outputs.
